QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_49

question.text: Which risk measure best captures TAIL risk beyond the confidence level, addressing a key limitation of Value at Risk?

explanation.text: The Logic: CVaR / Expected Shortfall averages the losses BEYOND the VaR threshold, capturing the tail depth that VaR ignores. It's superior for fat-tailed Cat III strategies (merger-arb, credit-arb, long-short with factor tilts). The Trap: A/B/D don't address tail loss magnitude. Cross-Exam Context: VIII Equity Derivatives, III-A/C Compliance test CVaR. XIX-E Cat III emphasises CVaR for fat-tail strategies. Manager's Pro-Tip: Report 95% VaR and 95% CVaR side-by-side to LPs. The ratio CVaR/VaR tells them how scary the tail is — a ratio > 1.5 = meaningful fat tail; LPs will ask questions.
